images.filename: USS Houston (CA-30) at Tjilatjap in February 1942.jpg
images.caption: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Houston (CA-30) at Tjilatjap, Java, 6 February 1942, seen from the light cruiser USS Marblehead (CL-12), which was passing close aboard. Houston 's colours are half-masted pending return of her funeral party, ashore for burial of men lost when a bomb hit near her after 20.3 cm gun turret two days earlier during a Japanese air attack in Bangka Strait. The disabled turret is visible in the center of the view, being trained to port.
images.alt: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Houston (CA-30) at Tjilatjap, Java, 6 February 1942, seen from the light cruiser USS Marblehead (CL-12), which was passing close aboard. Houston 's colours are half-masted pending return of her funeral party, ashore for burial of men lost when a bomb hit near her after 20.3 cm gun turret two days earlier during a Japanese air attack in Bangka Strait. The disabled turret is visible in the center of the view, being trained to port.

images.filename: USS Houston (CA-30) underway circa 1934.jpg
images.caption: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Houston (CA-30) underway circa 1934, with turrets 1 and 111 trained to port. Note that the ship is fitted with ramp on the side of the superstructure, visible below no. 2 turret. This was fitted for the convenience of the U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt when he travelled on board the ship. Roosevelt was suffering from paralytic illness.
images.alt: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Houston (CA-30) underway circa 1934, with turrets 1 and 111 trained to port. Note that the ship is fitted with ramp on the side of the superstructure, visible below no. 2 turret. This was fitted for the convenience of the U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt when he travelled on board the ship. Roosevelt was suffering from paralytic illness.

images.filename: USS Houston (CA-30) in the Gatun Locks, Panama Canal, on 5 August 1938 (NH 95257).jpg
images.caption: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Houston (CA-30) in the Gatun Locks, Panama Canal, 5 August 1938, with U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt bidding farewell to Panama's President F. H. Arosemena before sailing on the cruiser. Roosevelt is in the automobile just to left of the catapult. The destroyer USS McDougal (DD-358) is in the right background.
images.alt: The U.S. Navy heavy cruiser USS Houston (CA-30) in the Gatun Locks, Panama Canal, 5 August 1938, with U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt bidding farewell to Panama's President F. H. Arosemena before sailing on the cruiser. Roosevelt is in the automobile just to left of the catapult. The destroyer USS McDougal (DD-358) is in the right background.
images.artist: H.L. Brazeal, Fort Davis, Panama Canal Zone

images.filename: USS Houston CA-30 1938 (51107702288).jpg
images.caption:
USS Houston CA-30 getting underway from pier 18 at the US Navy base at Balboa in the canal zone in this early morning photo. she was heading for the Gatun Locks so President Franklin D. Roosevelt could bid farewell to Panama's President F. H. Arosemena.  President Roosevelt had attended a fleet review in San Francisco and was passing through the canal on his return to the east coast, the trip concluded at Pensacola FL on Aug 9th. ( note the Presidential flag on the aft mast ). Photo dates to the 5th of Aug, 1938

Credit International News Photos of NY
